text_blocks.snippet: Non-qualified retirement plans are employer-sponsored retirement plans that don't meet the requirements of ERISA (Employee Retirement Income Security Act). Unlike qualified plans, they offer flexibility in who can participate and often provide additional benefits to attract and retain key employees. They are commonly used by employers to offer additional retirement savings opportunities to highly compensated employees and executives.

list.title: Not subject to ERISA:
list.snippet: Non-qualified plans are not bound by the same rules and regulations regarding funding, reporting, and fiduciary obligations as qualified plans (like 401(k)s).

list.title: Flexibility in Design:
list.snippet: Employers have more freedom to customize eligibility, contributions, and benefits, making them useful for specific employee needs or as incentives.

list.title: Tax Implications:
list.snippet: Contributions to non-qualified plans may not be tax-deductible for the employer, but employees can defer taxes on contributions and investment growth until retirement.

list.title: Potential for Higher Contributions:
list.snippet: Non-qualified plans often allow employees to save more for retirement than qualified plans, particularly for those with higher incomes.

list.title: Risk for Employees:
list.snippet: Employees in non-qualified plans face a higher level of risk, as the benefits are not protected in the event of employer bankruptcy or financial difficulties.

list.title: Deferred Compensation Plans:
list.snippet: Allow employees to defer a portion of their salary or bonus to a later date, often in retirement.

list.title: Supplemental Executive Retirement Plans (SERPs):
list.snippet: Provide additional retirement benefits to executives, often beyond what's available in qualified plans.

list.title: Phantom Stock Plans:
list.snippet: Offer a cash benefit tied to the value of company stock, providing an incentive for performance.

list.title: Split-Dollar Life Insurance:
list.snippet: Share the cost and benefits of a life insurance policy between the employer and employee.

list.title: Executive Bonus Plans:
list.snippet: Provide a bonus to key employees that can be used for retirement savings or other purposes.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, non-qualified plans are a tool for employers to offer more tailored and potentially more lucrative retirement benefits to specific employees, while also providing a means to attract and retain key talent.
